label: GPT-6 Astra
output:
**To the neighbours on Aughrim Terrace,**

Someone has been putting full bags of their rubbish into my grey bin at No. 14, and I’ve had enough.

To be clear, this isn’t the odd wrapper or a few bits. It’s been full black bags, every week for about a month. Last Tuesday, I got home from work at 3am after a gig to find three bags that weren’t mine shoved into it, including one containing nappies. The lid wouldn’t even close.

I’m with Greenmount Bins and pay by weight, at 41 cent a kilo. My last bill was €63.20 for two months. It’s normally around €25. I’m not paying to get rid of someone else’s rubbish on top of my own.

The bin has **14 painted in white on the lid**, so there’s no confusion about whose it is. I put it out on Tuesday night for collection on Wednesday morning. That does not make it a free bin for anyone passing.

I work nights. Being out late doesn’t mean I won’t notice, and it certainly doesn’t mean I’m happy to put up with it. Whoever is doing this is leaving a neighbour to pick up their bill. Have a think about how you’d feel if it was your money.

If you’re stuck with your rubbish collection, ask. I’ll tell you who to ring. I’d much rather have that conversation than come home to another load of bags I’m expected to pay for.

**Whoever is doing this: stop using my bin.** If it carries on, I’ll be putting a padlock on it. I shouldn’t have to lock my own bin to avoid paying for somebody else’s waste.

Apologies to everyone getting this who has nothing to do with it. I don’t know who’s responsible, so I’m putting the same note through every door rather than pointing fingers.

**No. 14**
